anti_overlap: fd-pavement-survey-cadence: that agent focuses on interval choice for valid samples; this agent focuses on detecting and flagging where valid samples are absent
fd-agri-ndvi-aggregation: that agent focuses on aggregation bias given valid samples; this agent focuses on what happens when samples are missing or spatially incomplete
fd-mobile-airquality-calibration: that agent focuses on whether the raster values are trustworthy; this agent focuses on whether the raster spatially covers the graph
decision_lens: Is the spatial coverage of the shadow raster verified against the graph extent before the 95% NaN budget is spent, and is the NaN propagation path to Phase 1.6 fully specified?
distance_rationale: Hydrographic surveyors plan sounding lines to guarantee that no seafloor feature larger than a specified size goes undetected within a survey area — the same coverage-completeness requirement as ensuring that > 95% of graph edges have at least one valid shadow sample.
expected_isomorphisms: IHO S-44 distinguishes 'full seafloor search' from 'single beam' coverage, and defines coverage probability as a function of line spacing relative to feature size — this maps to the brainstorm's '> 95% edges receive non-NaN sun_fraction' acceptance criterion, which is a coverage-probability claim that should be derived from raster-extent vs. graph-extent geometry, not assumed.
focus: Missing-data and coverage-completeness handling — whether the NaN policy and the 95% acceptance criterion are justified by the spatial relationship between raster extent and graph extent
name: fd-hydro-survey-coverage
persona: Apply the perspective of a hydrographic survey planner who must certify that a survey achieves IHO S-44 Special Order coverage, tracking which areas have been sounded and which remain in shadow.
review_areas: The 95% non-NaN acceptance criterion assumes the DTLA bounding box is fully inside the DSM coverage — this is stated as a fact but never verified programmatically. A graph edge that extends 2 m outside the raster boundary will produce a mix of valid and clipped samples, passing the 95% gate while silently introducing aggregation bias

The shade_data_quality='no_coverage' flag is assigned only when every sample is nodata — but partial nodata (e.g., 8 of 11 samples are nodata) is not flagged and reduces the effective sample size without warning. IHO practice distinguishes 'gap' from 'insufficient density' coverage

The nodata value is read as src.nodata or 255 — if the GeoTIFF has src.nodata=None but the actual nodata fill is 255, the fallback is correct; if a future raster has src.nodata=0 (meaning no-data is encoded as 0, colliding with the 'sun' pixel value), the script will silently misclassify nodata as sun

The raster boundary clip guard (np.clip) means that samples falling outside the raster are mapped to boundary pixels rather than flagged as out-of-coverage — these produce false readings that pollute the valid-sample count and suppress the NaN flag on edges that should receive it

The idempotency check (mtime comparison) does not verify that the output graph's coverage statistics match the current raster — if the raster is regenerated with a different extent (e.g., after re-running build_shadow.py with a larger bbox), the existing output file is treated as fresh

No spatial audit report is produced to let the operator see which edges received NaN — the --report flag shows a distribution histogram but not a geographic extent or edge-ID list of no-coverage edges

severity_examples.example: If a future shadow raster encodes nodata as 0 (matching the 'sun' pixel value) and src.nodata is not set in the GeoTIFF metadata, every nodata pixel is silently counted as sun. The 95% non-NaN gate passes, sun_fraction values look plausible, and the routing layer receives systematically inflated sun fractions in uncovered areas. This is a silent data corruption mode with no error or warning.

The np.clip boundary guard converts out-of-raster sample coordinates to boundary pixel reads rather than marking them as nodata. Graph edges at the raster perimeter will have artificially high valid-sample counts, suppressing the NaN flag and producing sun_fraction values derived partly from a single boundary pixel repeated N times. The 95% acceptance criterion does not distinguish these 'covered by clip' edges from genuinely covered ones.

The shade_data_quality flag is only set on total-nodata edges. Edges with 50%+ nodata samples are indistinguishable from fully-covered edges in the output GraphML. IHO practice would log a 'reduced confidence' coverage class for these edges. Phase 1.6 has no signal that some non-NaN sun_fraction values rest on thin sample counts.

source_domain: Hydrographic survey line planning and IHO S-44 coverage standards
success_hints: Add a startup check: assert graph bounding box is fully contained within raster bounding box, exit 2 if not
Replace np.clip with explicit out-of-bounds detection — mask samples outside raster extent as nodata before computing sun_fraction
Store sun_valid_samples and sun_nodata_samples as edge attributes so coverage quality is inspectable
task_context: Phase 1.5 brainstorm for Solwend edge shadow sampling — fixed 5 m interval, vectorized NumPy raster lookup, NaN for no-coverage edges, sun_fraction drives felt-minute routing weight.
